on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161097926/
1 1.

The present appeal is filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined and award dated 30.07.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Amreli in MACP No.222 of 2009.

2. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellants - original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellants-original claimants entitled to an amount of Rs.2,60,754/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
Thus, the Tribunal has not entertained the claim petition for an amount of Rs.8,00,000/- as total compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1
On dated 04.05.2009, the husband of the appellant No.1 - Bablubhai had gone to village Khambha on his Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing No. GJ-14-L- 2784 for social work.

At about 6:00 pm, when he was returning to village Madhada driving the motorcycle with moderate speed, at that time, the driver of Tata 407 vehicle bearing No.
GJ-4-T-6674 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed with the motorcycle of the deceased, due to which Bablubhai received seriours injuries all over his body.

3.2 After the accident, injured - deceased Bablubhai was immediately taken to the Government Hospital, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined Khambha and was also shifted to Doctor House, Amreli, but owing to the nature of his serious injuries, he was shifted to Madhuram Hospital, Rajkot, where he was treated as an indoor patient and during the course of treatment of one and half months, he succumbed to the injuries.

entities.text: Government Hospital, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3.3 Therefore, the appellants - original claimants had filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with cost and interest against the respondents before the Tribunal.
3.4 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
4. This Court vide order dated 05.10.2011 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned advocate Mr. P.M. Lakhani, appearing for the appellants, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true Bablubhai Bavbhai Budhela Since Decd. ... vs Balabhai Hirabhai Rathod on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161097926/
2 perspective.

entities.text: Bablubhai Bavbhai Budhela Since Decd. ... vs Balabhai Hirabhai Rathod
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the prospective income of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined deceased as well as has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future prospects, loss of consortium and grant of compensation under the various heads such as loss of estate and funeral expenses.

6. It is further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the financial dependency of the family members and the socio-economic background of the deceased.
The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.
Learned counsel therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation amount by reassessing the same in accordance with law.

7. Learned advocate Mr. G.C. Mazmudar appearing for the respondent No.2- Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record,
awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.

8. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined perused impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.
9.

As regards the income of the deceased is concerned, who was doing agricultural work on his own land and is stated to be earning Rs. 4 Lakhs per year, the same is considered by the Tribunal as only Rs. 25,200/- per year (Rs.2100/- per month), which is on the lower side.
Hence, it is required to be changed to the tune of Rs. 3,000/- per month.

Moreover, as regards the future prospect is concerned, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the deceased in the Post- mortem report at Exhibit-40 is shown as 47 years but as per cross-examination of son of the deceased, same comes out as 50 years and from the claim petition, it is mentioned as 54 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though, the age of more than 60 years is accepted by the Tribunal, which cannot be considered by this Court towards towards the future prospects of the deceased.
Hence, the age of 54 years is to be considered, as mentioned in the claim petition, towards the future prospects of the deceased.
10. As rightly recorded by the Tribunal, considering the fact that the deceased was survived by widow and two sons, 1/3rd deduction has to be applied towards spend by the deceased on himself.

Thus, the calculation of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/08/2025 undefined prospective income of the deceased at the rate of 10% is to be considered as Rs.3,000/-*12= Rs.36,000/- and adding *10% of it (Rs.3,600/-) comes to Rs.39,600/-.

3 11.
After 1/3rd deduction towards personal expense of the deceased, the calculation of the income of the deceased is Rs.26,400/- (Rs.39,600/- - Rs.13,200/- (1/3rd deduction towards personal expenses).

Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 54 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the scheduled prescribed, the Tribunal has wrongly applied the multiplier of 5 in the facts of the case, which is required to be corrected by applying the multiplier of 11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the future loss benefit is determined as Rs.26,400/-*11 (Multiplier) which comes to Rs.2,90,400/-.
12.
This brings me to the issue of loss of consortium as prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants.

As rightly prayed for by the learned advocate for the appellants in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram & Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium to the tune of Rs.48,400/- for the widow.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram & Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Lastly, the amount to be awarded under the conventional heads, more NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined particularly,
funeral expenses and the loss of estate is also required to be reconsidered in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
The same is to be considered as Rs.18,150/- respectively.
The amount of Rs.1,53,754/- is rightly considered by the Tribunal towards medical expenses incurred.

13. Therefore, original claimants - appellants herein are entitled to enhanced amount as computed hereunder:
Compensation As per award As awarded by this under challenge Court (Rs.) (Rs.)
Actual salary/ 2,100/-*12= 3,000/-*12 = income 25,200/- p.a. 36,000/- p.a.
Prospective - +10% income (3,600) = 39,600/-
 Deduction 2/3 (16,800) 1/3   towards personal =26,400

expense - Loss of  Dependency  Future Loss 16,800*5 26,400*1  = 84,000/- = 2,90,4  For loss of 10,000/- 48,400/-
 consortium  (Wife)
 Loss of Estate 10,000/- 18,150/-
Funeral expenses 3,000/- 18,150/-
Medical Expenses 1,53,754/- 1,53,754

Total Rs.2,60,754/- Rs.5,28,

14.
For the foregoing reasons, the impugned judgment and award dated 30.07.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Amreli in MACP No.222 of 2009 hereby modified.
The appellants-original claimants are held entitled to compensation of an amount of Rs.5,28,854/-.

Since by impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.2,60,754/-, the appellants shall be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,68,100/-
(Rs.5,28,854/- - Rs.2,60,754/-) with interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization.

The respondent No. 2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation with proportionate costs and interest and recover the same from the Owner of the vehicle, as held by the tribunal.
15. Let, the aforesaid amount be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the present order.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to release and disburse the entire award amount in favour of the original claimant, after due verification as per the original judgment and award.

16. Let, such exercise be undertaken by the Tribunal strictly in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2703/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard; preferably within a period of two weeks from deposit of such amount.
The Tribunal is directed to realize the deficit Court fees before proceeding with the disbursement of the amount.
17. R&P be sent back to the concerned tribunal forthwith, if received.

Sd/-
